claims.claim: Use-case-specific queries stay in concrete repositories when an Infrastructure-only generic repository or base class is used.
claims.trigger: Implementing use-case-specific persistence queries in the path-scoped backend architecture, including use of an Infrastructure-only generic repository/base.
claims.exceptions: Generic Infrastructure helpers may remove real duplication; whether delegation to such helpers still counts as queries staying in concrete repositories is unresolved.
claims.enforcement_effect: Prose standard; no runtime enforcement asserted.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Generic base allowed only in Infrastructure for real duplication and retaining full EF Core are recorded, but query placement in concrete repositories is absent from their asserted actions. Quote overlap alone does not register this atom.

Cohesive specific interfaces, keeping query construction in Infrastructure and not replacing EF capabilities do not necessarily locate query implementation within concrete repositories rather than a subordinate Infrastructure query helper.

The quoted passage includes the clause, but the asserted finding is another generic CRUD contract prohibition and explicit repository injection. Its scenario/explanation does not assert query placement.

claims.comparison_reason: All-three action review of repository/interface/implementation/query records and exact-location coverage/policy records found no separately expressed concrete-repository query-placement clause. Potential independent restriction is source-grounded; whether it adds a meaningful restriction beyond concrete repository ownership while allowing internal helpers remains uncertain.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: Application uses a cohesive specific repository interface returning materialized results; the Infrastructure concrete repository delegates a tailored use-case EF query to an Infrastructure helper reused by another concrete repository. Full EF remains available and no query/provider types leak. The literal concrete-placement reading could reject this although the baseline boundary/generic-abstraction claims permit it; source does not settle ownership versus physical implementation.
claims.open_question: Does stay in concrete repositories constrain physical query placement/delegation independently, or only preserve concrete repository ownership already entailed by existing boundary clauses?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Family3 examine generic-base example and orphan classifications; family5 compare concrete method ownership versus internal query helpers without inferring a blanket helper ban.
